title: 1 Chronicles 6:50–65
context: 1 Chronicles 6:50–65 repeats Aaron’s line from Eleazar to Ahimaaz and then lists the cities given to the priests and the other Levitical families. The city list parallels Joshua 21, but the two differ. Chronicles places the Aaronite cities first and the summary after them, while Joshua 21:4–8 gives the summary first. Some names differ, such as Hilen and Holon, Ashan and Ain, and Allemeth and Almon (Joshua 21:15–18), and Chronicles does not list Juttah or Gibeon, though it still gives a total of thirteen priestly cities. Chronicles 6:61 reads briefly where Joshua 21:5 names Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. These notes name the differences and do not harmonize them. Both traditions read the list as God’s provision for the Levites, who received no tribal territory of their own.

verses.text: These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
verses.arminianNotes: Aaron’s sons are listed again: Eleazar, Phinehas, and Abishua. Arminians see the repetition reintroducing the priestly family before the list of priestly cities.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and read the repetition as a structural device. Both traditions note that the short list here repeats the first part of 6:4–8, preparing for the cities given to Aaron’s descendants.

verses.text: Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
verses.arminianNotes: The line continues with Bukki, Uzzi, and Zerahiah. Arminian readers see the same names as in 6:5–6, which reminds readers of the priestly succession.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the repeated names as a link between the genealogy and the city lists. Both traditions read the verse as part of a summary rather than a new record.

verses.text: Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
verses.arminianNotes: The line continues with Meraioth, Amariah, and Ahitub. Arminians note that this matches 6:6–7 and keeps the priestly line before the reader.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and treat the verse as a recap. Both traditions see the repetition as underlining the importance of the priestly family in the chapter’s structure.

verses.text: Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
verses.arminianNotes: The list ends with Zadok and Ahimaaz. Arminian readers see the short line ending in David’s and Solomon’s time, linking the priestly cities to the established priesthood of the united kingdom.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. The reason the list stops at Ahimaaz is not stated, and both traditions avoid speculating, reading the verse as a bridge to the city list that follows.

verses.text: Now these are their dwelling places according to their encampments in their borders: to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites (for theirs was the first lot),
verses.arminianNotes: These are the dwelling places of Aaron’s sons, of the Kohathite families, for theirs was the first lot. Arminians see God providing homes for those who served him, since the Levites received no tribal territory of their own.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the lot as an expression of God’s ordering. Both traditions note the parallel with Joshua 21:10, which also says the first lot fell to Aaron’s descendants.

verses.text: to them they gave Hebron in the land of Judah, and its pasture lands around it;
verses.arminianNotes: They gave them Hebron in Judah with its pasture lands. Arminian readers see Hebron, a city linked with Abraham and with Caleb, given to the priests, which honors their role in Israel.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and note the parallel with Joshua 21:11, which also calls the city Kiriath Arba. Both traditions read the verse as God’s provision for the priestly families.

verses.text: but the fields of the city and its villages, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
verses.arminianNotes: The fields and villages of the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh. Arminians see God honoring Caleb’s faithfulness, as promised in Joshua 14, while the priests receive the city itself.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the arrangement keeping both God’s promise to Caleb and his provision for the priests. Both traditions note the parallel with Joshua 21:12.

verses.text: To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge, Hebron, Libnah also with its pasture lands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Aaron’s sons received the cities of refuge, Hebron, and Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa. Arminian readers note that Hebron was the city of refuge in this group (Joshua 21:13), and they see the plural wording as a general description.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and do not harmonize the wording. Both traditions see the cities of refuge as God’s provision of justice and mercy for those who killed someone unintentionally (Numbers 35).

verses.text: Hilen with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Hilen and Debir with their pasture lands follow. Arminians note that Joshua 21:15 has Holon where Chronicles has Hilen, and they name the difference without trying to resolve it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the spelling difference as it stands. Both traditions read the verse as continuing the list of cities God provided for the priests.

verses.text: Ashan with its pasture lands, and Beth Shemesh with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: Ashan and Beth Shemesh with their pasture lands follow. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:16 has Ain where Chronicles has Ashan, and that Joshua also lists Juttah, which Chronicles does not include here.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the differences without harmonizing them. Both traditions read the verse as part of the record of priestly cities in Judah and Simeon.

verses.text: and out of the tribe of Benjamin, Geba with its pasture lands, Allemeth with its pasture lands, and Anathoth with its pasture lands. All their cities throughout their families were thirteen cities.
verses.arminianNotes: From Benjamin come Geba, Allemeth, and Anathoth, and the total is thirteen cities. Arminians note that Joshua 21:17–18 lists Gibeon and Almon, and that Chronicles names fewer cities while giving the same total.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the difference unharmonized. Both traditions recall that Anathoth was later Jeremiah’s hometown (Jeremiah 1:1), a priestly city that produced a prophet.

verses.text: To the rest of the sons of Kohath were given by lot, out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.
verses.arminianNotes: The rest of Kohath received ten cities by lot from the half-tribe of Manasseh. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:5 also names Ephraim and Dan, and that Chronicles reads more briefly here.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and do not attempt to reconstruct the wording. Both traditions read the verse as recording God’s provision for the remaining Kohathite families.

verses.text: To the sons of Gershom, according to their families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Gershom’s families received thirteen cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan. Arminians see the Levites spread through the northern tribes, matching Joshua 21:6.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see God placing Levites among many tribes so that his worship and teaching could reach them all. Both traditions read the verse as shared ground.

verses.text: To the sons of Merari were given by lot, according to their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Merari’s families received twelve cities by lot from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. Arminian readers see God’s provision reaching even the tribes east of the Jordan, matching Joshua 21:7.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the lot as God’s ordering. Both traditions note that the Levites’ spread throughout the land served the whole nation.

verses.text: The children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: The children of Israel gave the Levites the cities with their pasture lands. Arminians see the tribes obeying God’s command (Numbers 35:1–8) by sharing their inheritance with the Levites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the gift as both obedience and God’s provision. Both traditions read the verse as a reminder that the whole community supported those who served at the sanctuary.

verses.text: They gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities which are mentioned by name.
verses.arminianNotes: They gave by lot from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin the cities named. Arminian readers note that this summary refers back to the priestly cities already listed in 6:57–60, while Joshua 21:9 places a similar statement before the list.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the difference in order without harmonizing it. Both traditions read the verse as confirming that these cities were assigned by lot under God’s direction.
